hypothesis: Within one species, heads (or cones) carrying a given parastichy pair are split about equally between the two chiralities: the larger parastichy family runs clockwise in roughly half of specimens and anticlockwise in the other half, as in Thompson's 224 right-handed versus 243 left-handed among 467 five-eight spruce cones.
pass_criterion: Pre-registered. In the Turing's Sunflowers data (Helianthus annuus), restrict to heads with both a clockwise and an anticlockwise parastichy count that together form an adjacent pair of one Fibonacci-type sequence (Fibonacci, Lucas, double Fibonacci or F4, as defined by Swinton et al. 2016). Define a head as right-handed when its larger family is clockwise. Pooled over all such heads, the proportion p of right-handed heads must satisfy |p - 0.5| <= 0.10 and a two-sided exact binomial test against 0.5 must give P >= 0.05. In addition, in each pair class with n >= 20 heads, |p - 0.5| <= 0.15 or the binomial P >= 0.05. Primary counts are the photoreviewed counts (author's annotation file); the submitter counts are a secondary replication.
fail_criterion: Pre-registered. Pooled |p - 0.5| > 0.10 with two-sided exact binomial P < 0.01 (a substantial and significant excess of one chirality), or the same pattern in the two most frequent pair classes. Any other outcome is 'mixed' (e.g. a small but significant bias with |p - 0.5| <= 0.10) or 'inconclusive' (fewer than 100 usable heads: underpowered).
interpretation: Thompson's 'direction' of the five-series (right- versus left-handed spiral) is mapped to the chirality of the larger parastichy family of a Fibonacci-type pair, scored as clockwise or anticlockwise in a fixed viewing convention (the seed face of the head as photographed). Thompson's own counts are of Norway spruce cones; no public per-cone table of those counts exists, so the test is a replication in another phyllotactic system (sunflower capitula), which the claim explicitly extends to ('phyllotactic systems generally'). Thompson's own 224:243 split is reported alongside for comparison but is not used as data.

datasets.role: chirality of the larger parastichy family in Helianthus annuus heads

method: fetch.py downloads the two spreadsheets (Dryad serves them behind a browser proof-of-work challenge; the files were obtained with headless Chrome, checksummed, and a 49 KB derived table committed under derived/). analysis.py parses the photoreviewed counts (best estimate before any parenthesised range), keeps heads whose two counts are adjacent members of the Fibonacci, Lucas, double-Fibonacci or F4 sequence, and scores a head right-handed if the larger family is clockwise. The proportion right-handed is tested against 0.5 with a two-sided exact binomial test, pooled and within each pair class; the submitter counts are analysed the same way as a replication.

measured.unit: proportion of heads whose larger parastichy family runs clockwise (photoreviewed counts)

caveats: The test is on sunflower capitula, not on the Norway spruce cones Thompson cites; his spruce tally is not available as a per-cone dataset and was not re-analysed.

The sample is a citizen-science collection of mostly one cultivated species grown in many gardens; counts are subjective, but handedness (which family is larger and which way it runs) is robust to small count errors.

Heads whose two counts did not form an adjacent Fibonacci-type pair (about 40% of photoreviewed heads with two counts) were excluded by the pre-registered rule; chirality in disordered heads is not tested.

The 21/34 class (n = 29) leans right-handed (20:9, P = 0.06); it passes the pre-registered class rule only through its P value, and the two large classes lean in opposite directions, consistent with chance.
The pass criterion tolerates a true bias of up to 10 percentage points; the 95% CI (0.465-0.586) excludes biases larger than about 9 points in either direction.
